thread:
nina: FYI customer 'Payflux' reporting intermittent failures on embeddings -> indexing. they see 'vector length mismatch' errors in our indexer and rows are being dropped. started ~07:20 UTC. :frowning:

nina: stack trace from their side pasted below, they said it happens after a big client-side model switch.

nina: ```
ERROR: indexer: reject row id=usr_8923 reason=vector_len(1024) != expected(1536)
caused_by: client_sent_model=gpt-embed-2x v2.1 -> previous=gpt-embed-3x v1.9
```

devon: thanks, adding context: their traffic has a mix of short/long conversation summaries + user bios, so embeddings vary. but indexer has a single expected vector width (1536). sounds like client changed model without pinning.

elaine: can we see request samples? nina, did they share any request payloads or batch headers?

nina: they gave a repro curl and a snippet. pasted:

nina: ```
curl -X POST https://inference.redwood.com/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-embed-2x","input":["summary A","summary B"]}'
```

lee: quick triage: if the embed endpoint returns mixed-length outputs in the same batch (e.g., an older client sends one model name and then another for the same bulk request) our indexer consumer currently validates length per-batch and rejects the entire batch when they differ. that's to avoid corrupting vector DB mappings.

devon: two failure modes here: 1) client-side accidentally sent a mixed-model batch (rare but possible) 2) client switched default model globally mid-stream and backoff retried different model. we should capture which one.

sam: billing note: they opened a dispute — thousands of rejected rows triggered a backfill run, which consumed dedicated capacity and bumped their invoice. asking for credit for the backfill attempt. billing-bot please tag relevant invoice.

billing-bot: noted. invoice: INV-2026-0387 flagged for review, customer request created.

elaine: repro plan: 1) ask for raw request headers+body with model field for the failing window 2) check our embed service logs for mixture of model identifiers 3) see whether the indexer could be adjusted to accept a co-existence migration (two widths) while we backfill.

nina: customer provided one more log with a timestamped request id: req_0ab3, req_0ab4, req_0ab7. two of those returned 1024 vectors and one returned 1536.

devon: OK I'll pull the inference logs for those request ids and the ingress batching_trace. probably we can tell whether the create-batch routine combined differently tagged requests. assigning to devon.

devon: (10m later) quick find: req_0ab3 model=gpt-embed-2x -> 1024, req_0ab4 model=gpt-embed-3x -> 1536. they had a single client connection that altered default model between calls. our batching window collapsed them into a single batch because headers only differ in model field.

elaine: so the root cause: server-side batching combined payloads from the same connection across model versions. that's an ops bug: batching key wasn't including model id.

lee: action items: (A) short-term: update indexer to fail fast but surface per-row diagnostics so customers can see which rows were dropped (B) immediate hotfix: change batching key to include model identifier to avoid cross-model mixes (C) mid-term: support dual-dimension migration mode in indexer for staged backfills.

sam: customer is asking for an emergency patch and a partial refund for the backfill. liaising with sales/CS.

nina: proposed hotfix already staged on canary: patch to batching routine adds model tag; rolling to one region now. DeployBot: status?

indexer-bot: deploy started for patch/embedding-batch-key to canary-1 at 09:18 UTC. health checks OK so far.

devon: while patch rolls, can we provide a temporary workaround: instruct clients to pin model name in each request and avoid sending mixed batches. share sample client-side guard:

devon: ```
# python example: ensure single-model batches
batch = []
current_model = None
for record in inputs:
    if current_model is None:
        current_model = record['model']
    if record['model'] != current_model:
        send_batch(batch)  # flush
        batch = []
        current_model = record['model']
    batch.append(record['text'])
send_batch(batch)
```

elaine: backfill strategy: we can run a staged reingest for the dropped ids. two options: (1) rerun embeddings production with pinned model (1536) and reindex into new namespace, keep both namespaces for a week and switch reads (2) adapt indexer to accept 1024 vectors into a separate column and run transform. option 1 is safer.

sam: customer prefers option 1 since they want consistent vector widths. they also asked for a runbook to avoid recurrence.

lee: notes for postmortem: batching key must include model & model-version hash; indexer should log rejected ids with the actual length and expected length; also add an alert when rejected rate > 0.1% per minute.

devon: follow-ups: I'll post PR and link to canary logs. nina, please ask customer for the full list of failed ids and permission to reingest.

nina: will do, pinging the Payflux contact now.

nina: customer responded: approves reingest for ids listed, requests credit for compute spent. CS asks for a goodwill credit covering the backfill job minus any normal usage.

sam: accepted, tagging finance for credit approval. finance please confirm.

lee: reminder: we should also check whether our SDKs ever hide model field or normalize it — if an SDK switched internal model mapping unexpectedly that could be root cause for other customers.

devon: good call. I'll search repo history for last SDK release that touched default model mapping.

indexer-bot: canary deploy finished at 09:33 UTC. no regressions observed in 15m smoke tests.

elaine: next steps summary (assign owners): devon -> infra logs + PR to include model-id in batching key; lee -> alerting + indexer rejection diagnostics; nina -> customer coord + get failed id list; sam -> billing/credit negotiation; elaine -> plan backfill run and keep read-coexistence plan.

nina: thanks all, customer on a call at 10:00 UTC. will update thread after reingest signoff. :thumbsup:
